title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: All executive and non-executive directors of Reece Limited and its subsidiaries. Subject to black-out periods, the three month short-term dealing ban, prior written clearance from the Chair or Company Secretary (Chair of the Board from the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee), immediate notification of buys and sells to the Company Secretary for ASX disclosure, and the section 6.2 hedging regime.

tiers.name: Executives
tiers.description: Employees who are members of the Executive Leadership Teams, and/or receive equity awards or any form of equity under any Group Long Term Incentive Plan, and/or hold a position which makes them a Director or Officer of any Group company under the Corporations Act. Subject to the same additional restrictions as Directors, with clearance from the MD and Group CEO or Company Secretary, plus a specific bar on hedging Plan equity awards before exercise or while subject to a transfer restriction.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All employees of the Company and its subsidiaries. Outside black-out periods, Employees other than Directors and Executives may deal without clearance provided they hold no inside information. The three month short-term dealing ban still applies to them; the section 6 clearance and hedging provisions do not.

tiers.name: Related Parties
tiers.description: A spouse, domestic partner, child (under 18) or dependent of the person, a child or dependent of their spouse or domestic partner, any other family member who may be expected to influence or be influenced by the person, or a company, trust, partnership or other entity that the person or those persons control or significantly influence. For clause 6.1 purposes a reference to Directors and Executives is also a reference to their Related Parties.

definitions.hedging_definition: hedging includes the entry into any transaction, arrangement or financial product which operates to limit the economic risk of a security holding in the Company and includes financial instruments such as equity swaps and contracts for differences

windows.start_anchor: 1 January (half year results, released in February)
1 July (full year results, released in August)
1 October (first quarter update at the Annual General Meeting)
windows.end_anchor: the day of the Annual General Meeting (inclusive)

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may designate any other period as a black-out period; it must be advised to Employees, and Employees are notified of black-out periods through a notification posted to the Company intranet, so ad hoc blackouts are communicated internally rather than kept confidential. Separately, the Company may notify a person in writing that certain company securities cannot be traded for a specified period.

rules.detail: The policy expressly contemplates derivatives over Reece shares by permitting Directors to hedge their shareholdings, with equity swaps and contracts for differences named as examples of hedging instruments. Entry, renewal, alteration and close-out each require compliance with clause 6.1: advance written notice, written clearance acknowledgement from the Chair or Company Secretary, outside a black-out period, and no price sensitive information. There is no venue restriction, so an over-the-counter put and call with a bank are within the permission.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives are only permitted to hedge their shareholdings: In compliance with section 6.1 above; and Providing the hedge transaction is not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information.

rules.detail: Same position as Directors for shares that have been acquired on exercise and are free of any transfer restriction, except clearance comes from the MD and Group CEO or Company Secretary.
rules.evidence: Executives must give advance notice and receive clearance acknowledgement (e.g. by way of exchange of emails) from the MD and Group CEO or Company Secretary before commencing to deal in Company Securities

rules.detail: Employees who are not Directors or Executives are outside the section 6 clearance and hedging provisions. They may deal outside black-out periods without inside information and without clearance; the three month short-term dealing ban in 5.3 still binds them, and forward contracts are named there as prohibited short-term dealings.
rules.evidence: At any time other than during a black-out period, Employees (other than Directors and Executives) may deal in securities in the Company but only if you do not have inside information.

rules.detail: Hedging of a Director's shareholding is expressly permitted, subject only to clause 6.1 clearance and to the requirement that entry, renewal, alteration and close-out do not occur while holding price sensitive information. The bar on hedging Plan equity awards is directed at Executives; a Director who receives Plan equity would also meet the 'Executives' definition and be caught by it. There is no absolute hedging prohibition anywhere in the policy.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives are only permitted to hedge their shareholdings: In compliance with section 6.1 above; and Providing the hedge transaction is not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information.

rules.detail: Absolute bar on hedging equity awards granted under a Plan before the rights are exercised. No clearance route and no exceptional circumstances relief.
rules.evidence: However, Executives are not permitted to hedge equity awards granted under a Plan prior to exercising those rights or, once exercised, while the securities are subject to a transfer restriction.

rules.detail: The bar continues after exercise for as long as the resulting securities are subject to a transfer restriction, so shares still inside a holding lock cannot be collared.
rules.evidence: or, once exercised, while the securities are subject to a transfer restriction.

rules.detail: Once Plan awards have been exercised and the resulting securities are free of any transfer restriction, the specific bar falls away and the general permission applies: hedging is allowed with clearance from the MD and Group CEO or Company Secretary, outside black-out periods and with no price sensitive information at entry, renewal, alteration or close-out.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executives are only permitted to hedge their shareholdings: In compliance with section 6.1 above

rules.detail: Section 6.2 regulates hedging only by Directors and Executives. The policy says nothing about hedging by other Employees, who are otherwise free to deal outside black-out periods without inside information.

Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, collar or similar is a transaction, arrangement or financial product operating to limit the economic risk of a Reece shareholding and so is hedging, permitted with clause 6.1 clearance. The counterweight is clause 5.3, which gives forward contracts as an example of prohibited short-term dealings, so a short-dated monetisation is at risk of being characterised as prohibited short-term dealing.
rules.evidence: hedging includes the entry into any transaction, arrangement or financial product which operates to limit the economic risk of a security holding in the Company

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the policy and there is no prohibited dealings list. Only the three month short-term dealing ban and the insider trading prohibition would apply.
Securities lending is not named and is not caught by the section 4.1 description of trading or dealing, which is confined to buying, selling, subscribing and agreements to do so.

Contracts for differences are expressly named as an example of a hedging instrument, so a CFD over a Director's or Executive's shareholding is permitted with clause 6.1 clearance. A CFD closed out within three months would engage the short-term dealing ban, and an Executive may not use one over unvested or transfer-restricted Plan securities.
rules.evidence: includes financial instruments such as equity swaps and contracts for differences.

rules.detail: Margin lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy, for any tier or security state, and there is no requirement to notify or obtain approval for it.

Granting security, a charge, mortgage, lien or pledge over Company securities is not mentioned, and the section 4.1 description of trading or dealing (buy, sell, subscribe, or agree to do so) does not sweep it in.
The policy contains no secured financing provision of any kind: no ban, no clearance requirement, no disclosure obligation and no guidance on forced sales by a lender during a black-out period.

Directors and Employees must not round-trip Company securities within three months in either direction, and must not enter into any other short-term dealings, with forward contracts given as an express example. No stated matching basis and no carve-out for Plan securities or for the exercise of equity awards.
rules.evidence: Directors and Employees must not buy and sell or sell and buy securities in the Company within a three-month period or enter into any other short-term dealings in Company securities (for example, forward contracts).

clearance.approver: Chair or Company Secretary for Directors other than the Chair of the Board; Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Chair of the Board
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary, so the Company can inform the ASX as required by law
clearance.post_trade_deadline: immediately when they buy or sell shares in the Company
clearance.evidence: Directors (other than the Chair of the Board) must give advance written notice and receive written clearance acknowledgement (e.g. by way of exchange of emails) from the Chair or Company Secretary before commencing to deal in Company Securities ... Directors and Executives who are given written clearance to deal in accordance with the Policy must deal as soon as possible and in any event within 5 business days

clearance.approver: MD and Group CEO or Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: Executives must give advance notice and receive clearance acknowledgement (e.g. by way of exchange of emails) from the MD and Group CEO or Company Secretary before commencing to deal in Company Securities (which must only occur outside a black-out period and the Executive confirms that he or she is not in possession of inside information)

clearance.approver: The same approver as for the associated Director or Executive, who must communicate on the Related Party's behalf
clearance.evidence: For the purpose of this clause 6.1, a reference to 'Directors' and 'Executives' is also a reference to their Related Parties. ... Communication on behalf of those persons with relevant person for the purpose of this Policy (e.g. to obtain approval as required by the clearance procedures in clause 6.1)
At any time other than during a black-out period, Employees (other than Directors and Executives) may deal in securities in the Company but only if you do not have inside information.

short_term.basis: buy and sell or sell and buy within a three-month period; extended to 'any other short-term dealings', with forward contracts given as an example
short_term.evidence: Directors and Employees must not buy and sell or sell and buy securities in the Company within a three-month period or enter into any other short-term dealings in Company securities (for example, forward contracts).

exceptions.evidence: Where you are not in possession of price sensitive information and there exists exceptional circumstances such as severe financial difficulties or passive trades (such as sales compelled by law) you may apply in writing to the Company Secretary for approval to dispose of (but not to acquire) Company securities during a black-out period.
exceptional circumstances such as severe financial difficulties or passive trades (such as sales compelled by law)
Vested equity awards held pursuant to a Plan may be exercised in accordance with the relevant Plan rules. The exercise of equity awards may occur within a black-out period.
On receipt of securities on automatic conversion or grant (for example on satisfaction of performance conditions on an equity award);
any sale of securities in the Company acquired upon exercise of equity awards may only occur ... During a black-out period, with written permission from the Company Secretary.

external_documents: Group Long Term Incentive Plan rules
exemption_authority: The Company Secretary may, on written application, approve the disposal (but not the acquisition) of Company securities during a black-out period where the person holds no price sensitive information and there are exceptional circumstances such as severe financial difficulties or passive trades such as sales compelled by law; such approvals are valid for three business days. The Company Secretary may also give written permission for the sale during a black-out period of securities acquired on exercise of equity awards. No one is given authority to waive the three month short-term dealing ban or the bar on Executives hedging unvested or transfer-restricted Plan securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Executives are only permitted to hedge their shareholdings: In compliance with section 6.1 above; and Providing the hedge transaction is not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a permission rather than a prohibition, so the derivative legs of a collar over a Director's or Executive's shareholding are allowed provided each of entry, renewal, alteration and close-out is separately cleared and clean of price sensitive information.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, charges, pledges or encumbrances over Company securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is neither prohibited nor made subject to clearance or disclosure, so the funded element of the structure is not blocked by the policy, though the bank should still confirm the position with the Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy is silent on sales of Company securities effected by a third party such as a secured lender, and there is no excluded dealing for them.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A lender enforcement sale or physical settlement falling inside a black-out period has no safe harbour, and the only relief route is a discretionary Company Secretary approval for a disposal on exceptional circumstances grounds.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Employees must not buy and sell or sell and buy securities in the Company within a three-month period or enter into any other short-term dealings in Company securities (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Forward-style monetisation is expressly given as an example of a prohibited short-term dealing, so the collar tenor and any roll or unwind should comfortably exceed three months and the structure should be documented as a hedge rather than a forward sale.

bespoke_clauses.clause: However, Executives are not permitted to hedge equity awards granted under a Plan prior to exercising those rights or, once exercised, while the securities are subject to a transfer restriction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar can only reference shares acquired on exercise that are free of any transfer restriction, so the eligible parcel must be verified against Plan records before pricing.

bespoke_clauses.topic: close-out is a separate cleared event
bespoke_clauses.clause: Providing the hedge transaction is not entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Director or Executive is in possession of price sensitive information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Renewal, amendment and termination of the collar each require the person to be clean of price sensitive information and, under clause 6.1, to be cleared and outside a black-out period, so the documentation should avoid automatic or counterparty-triggered close-outs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Can be given or refused by Reece in its discretion, without giving any reasons; Can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances; Reece's discretion to refuse clearance is final and binding.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance can be revoked between grant and execution and a refusal cannot be explained to the bank, so there is execution risk in the five business day window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance under this clause is not an endorsement of proposed trading and it is the Directors and Executives whom are ultimately responsible for ensuring their dealings in securities comply with the applicable laws and as applicable, the Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A clearance acknowledgement should not be treated by the bank as a company confirmation that the collar is compliant; the risk stays with the individual.

bespoke_clauses.clause: For the purpose of this clause 6.1, a reference to 'Directors' and 'Executives' is also a reference to their Related Parties. ... A company, trust, partnership or another entity that the person or any of the persons referred to in the above bullet points controls or significantly influences.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar entered through a family trust or controlled company still requires clearance, and the Director or Executive must communicate with the approver on that entity's behalf.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If you possess price sensitive information in relation to an entity you cannot 'trade' or 'deal' in the following ways: Buy or sell securities in that entity or subscribe for new securities; or Enter into an agreement to subscribe for, buy or sell securities in that entity.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The general dealing definition does not sweep in derivatives, encumbrances or stock lending; derivatives are regulated only through the separate section 6.2 hedging regime, which is a permission, so the policy's restrictive reach over an OTC collar is narrow.

bespoke_clauses.clause: you may apply in writing to the Company Secretary for approval to dispose of (but not to acquire) Company securities during a black-out period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The exceptional circumstances relief is disposal-only, so a collar entry (which involves acquiring a put) cannot be cleared inside a black-out period on hardship grounds.

summary: A funded collar is available to Reece Directors and Executives, on conditions, and this policy is unusually permissive. Section 6.2 expressly permits Directors and Executives to hedge their shareholdings, defining hedging to include any transaction, arrangement or financial product limiting the economic risk of a Reece holding and naming equity swaps and contracts for differences, with no venue restriction, so an over-the-counter put and call with a bank are contemplated. The conditions are prior written clearance under clause 6.1 (Chair or Company Secretary for Directors, Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Chair of the Board, MD and Group CEO or Company Secretary for Executives), execution within five business days, dealing outside the 1 January, 1 July and 1 October black-out periods, no price sensitive information at entry, renewal, alteration or close-out, and immediate notification by Directors to the Company Secretary for ASX disclosure. The loan leg is not obstructed: the policy says nothing at all about margin lending, secured financing, charges or pledges over Company securities, and imposes no related disclosure, although it equally gives no safe harbour for a lender's forced sale during a black-out period. The collar must reference shares that are not unvested Plan awards or subject to a transfer restriction, and its tenor, roll and unwind should exceed three months because clause 5.3 bans short-term dealings and gives forward contracts as an example.
